You are one of 4 members of a group that stays together for 10 rounds.

Every round, all members act at the same time: each receives 20 tokens and splits them between their own account and the group account, using the split tool once.
- Each token in your own account pays you 1 point.
- Each token in the group account pays 0.3 points to every member of the group, you included, whoever put it there.

After each round you learn how many tokens the group account received in total and how many points you got. You never learn what any other member did.

calls.text: Round 1 of 10.

reply.thinking:
This is a classic public goods game setup: each token contributed returns only 0.3 to the contributor but 1.2 to the group total, so self-interest favors contributing nothing while full cooperation (everyone contributing all 20 tokens) yields 24 points each versus 20 for universal defection. The tension is clear — socially optimal behavior conflicts with individually rational behavior.

I'm weighing whether to signal cooperative intent with a moderate contribution rather than going fully selfish or fully altruistic. Since this is round one of ten with no visibility into others' individual choices, I'll open with a moderate contribution of 10 tokens — enough to test reciprocity without being overly exploitable.

Rather than fully free-riding or fully cooperating, I'll start with a moderate contribution of 10 to signal willingness to cooperate without risking total exploitation as a sole cooperator, leaving room to adjust based on how others behave.
